dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Somehow, everyone in this story ends up being nice...

dialogues.speaker: Ignatov
dialogues.text: ...My parents only worry because I've always been frail. They don't want me working and getting sick.

dialogues.speaker: Ignatov
dialogues.text: And Tolstaya wants me to read something else because she thinks... heh, these books are making me gloomy.

dialogues.speaker: Ignatov
dialogues.text: I know they care about me. They've always protected me, and I'm grateful for that. But... I'm sorry. Maybe I really am strange...

dialogues.speaker: Ignatov
dialogues.text: I keep wanting to go outside — to step out of this warm, gentle spring and into the freezing ice pit myself.

dialogues.speaker: Ignatov
dialogues.text: Mr. Zheleznov said it meant I was looking for a kind of growth that was mine and mine alone. Then he handed me a huge stack of books and said maybe I'd find the answer in them...

dialogues.speaker: Ignatov
dialogues.text: And then... hehe, Tolstaya came over with her hands on her hips and showed him out. He even made a face at me on his way out.

dialogues.speaker: Ignatov
dialogues.text: ...Ah! I-I really shouldn't be standing here chatting. I need to get back to work. I'm sorry. If you need anything, please just call me.
